hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. It was the only Florida city selected.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has been selected as one of only 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the sole Florida city honored this year. The award was presented during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where city leaders showcased their efforts to strengthen community involvement and collaboration. The recognition celebrates communities that unite residents, government, businesses and organizations to address local challenges and drive meaningful change.

Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the recognition, describing Riviera Beach as "one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He emphasized that the award reflects a sustained commitment to revitalize the city and enhance residents' quality of life. Lawson noted that community members are witnessing the transformation and reimagining of Riviera Beach that leaders have pursued for years. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents directly for the honor, stating that the award belongs to the entire community because residents show up for one another through events, projects and challenges. She added that the designation reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride.

The city's application highlighted three key civic engagement programs. The Riviera Beach Youth Council enables high school students to participate in civic leadership and advocacy. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education program, boasts a 98 percent completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants to longtime homeowners for necessary repairs. City leaders emphasized that these initiatives represent a broader commitment to treating civic engagement as an ongoing partnership between government, residents, faith groups, schools and community organizations. Miller-Anderson noted that the city is implementing innovative programs to ensure residents feel they are part of shaping their community's future.

The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors. Being selected positions Riviera Beach for future opportunities and continued growth. City officials said the designation sends a message to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration produces results and residents remain deeply engaged in determining their community's direction. The other nine cities receiving the award are Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher who was suspended last year for social media comm.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying numerous findings are not based upon competent substantial evidence. The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a serious offense and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page within a discussion among personal acquaintances and were not intended for public view. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back, with no clear timeline for a final decision.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of operating anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts critical of Governor Ron DeSantis were suddenly deactivated Friday after prominent DeSantis communications veterans publicly accu.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. The accusations came from prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team, including Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email address similar to those known to be used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which displayed messages to an email address with letters starred out and a phone number showing only the last digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that also appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw noted that the account content consisted entirely of posts promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. She pointed out that a member of a state board appointed by the same governor she was criticizing would presumably be too busy to maintain such accounts. Redfern posted that the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public accusations. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys two boats for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County maritime teams are on standby with two boats and medics positioned in the north and south as hundreds of boaters hit the water for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting Martin County Maritime Response Unit to deploy two boats with medics on standby in both the north and south areas of the county. Lt. Brett Harry said his team is prepared to respond to a wide range of medical emergencies, from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious cardiac events, potential spinal injuries and other critical situations.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, are taking extra precautions on the water. Harry emphasized that boaters should keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Secretary of State seeks to keep Republican candidate off ballot after incomplete qualifying papers
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to bar Paula Stark from the House District 47 ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork by the June 12 qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Paula Stark submitted her qualifying materials just 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12, and now Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep the St. Cloud Republican off the ballot. Five state employees provided sworn written declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the required Form 6 and did not receive it back when he turned in the rest of the paperwork during the final moments of the qualifying window. More than three weeks after the deadline, Stark still has not provided Form 6, according to a court disclosure by Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve.

Byrd challenged Stark's claims about a paperwork mix-up in his court response, suggesting she could have prevented the problem with more care. "Had Candidate Stark or Treasurer Davis exercised the slightest degree of care or prudence in the matter by questioning why the Form 6 was allegedly handed back, the mistake would have been discovered while Treasurer Davis was at the Division," Byrd wrote. He also noted that waiting until the last moment to file created unnecessary risk. Form 6 is a public disclosure form for financial interests. Reeve noted that Stark was one of 12 candidates who failed to properly submit Form 6, but half of those candidates corrected the problem and still qualified for the ballot.

Beyond the missing Form 6, Reeve documented a pattern of campaign finance problems. Stark's treasurer filed a campaign finance report more than one month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. In the 2022 and 2024 election cycles, audits found inconsistent transfers between accounts and balance problems. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines, with a remaining fine referred to debt collection for nonpayment.

The timing of this decision matters significantly. Byrd noted that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots due out between July 9 and 16. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the House District 47 primary would become an open contest between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. This would represent a major advantage for Florida Democrats, as the traditionally blue district representing parts of Osceola and Orange counties saw no other Republican candidates file to run. Byrd argued that reversing course at this stage would be costly and could create confusion in election results.

cards.headline: Juno Beach debates fence replacement at JB-7 beach access after residents report trespassing
cards.teaser: Colony Condos residents say people using the JB-7 public beach access have been cutting through their private property since the town removed a boundary fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
cards.body:
A dispute over a missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point has created tension between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with a potential fix that could cost the town thousands of dollars. Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway have been cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without the barrier, only bushes now separate the public access path from private land, leaving residents frustrated by what they describe as repeated trespassing incidents.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem intensifies during summer months when beachgoers arrive to use the public access point. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Hill explained that residents previously confronted trespassers directly but have since shifted to calling police after encountering hostile responses from beachgoers. She said the fence once made the boundary between public and private property clearly visible.

The issue reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where officials acknowledged the town is not legally obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring lower-cost alternatives rather than a full replacement. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. Hill indicated that residents hope the town will reinstall the original fence to restore their landscaping and private parking areas. The council agreed to address the fence question during upcoming budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

Not all beachgoers perceive the situation as problematic. Michael House, who walks to JB-7 from a public parking lot blocks away, said he has not witnessed the issues residents describe. "There's plenty of free parking. If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue," House said. "I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that." His perspective highlights the divide in how different users view the public beach access point and whether a fence replacement is truly necessary to address the concerns raised by condo residents.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to march in National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march down the National Mall on July 4, representing Florida in Washington D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event. Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the magnitude of the moment, noting that millions, if not billions, of people will be watching. She emphasized the physical demands of marching band, explaining that students must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound.

Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is focused on nailing the marching and timing of everything, knowing that everyone will see what the Boca High band is capable of. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed full confidence in her students to put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer called getting to perform in D.C. an amazing opportunity that shows how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those who want to cheer on the band from home.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. School districts and schools receive letter grades from the Florida Department of Education based on student performance on state tests, graduation rates and student performance on advanced coursework. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, were rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5 percent graduation rate, with 86 percent of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the biggest success stories came from Delray Beach, where S.D. Spady Elementary School made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating to an "A" rating. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years as principal and five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround by modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program three years ago, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark's insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for a breast reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
A recently diagnosed breast cancer patient and her surgeon are speaking out after her insurance company denied coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy, but Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for her reconstruction surgery using a surgical mesh called GalaFlex. According to the denial letter, the surgery is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that is popular among plastic surgeons but not FDA-approved for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Despite the insurance denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago through Billington's efforts. Last year, after WPTV's investigative reporting as part of the "Patient No More" series, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem responded to Clark's denial by stating the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval, though she has the right to appeal.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4 percent this year
cards.teaser: According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July means cookouts, grilling and picnics, and this year, that tradition comes with a higher price tag. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation. Ground beef is up 5.5 percent, and buns are up 7.7 percent. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4 percent. Ice cream is up 5.3 percent.

Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check by shopping savvier than ever and comparing stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list. Woroch emphasized that the biggest thing for families is cutting down food waste, and that begins with a meal plan.

hero.headline: Juno Beach fence dispute at JB-7 beach access could cost town thousands
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
hero.body:
A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating conflict between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with potential costs to the town reaching into six figures. Residents at the Colony Condos claim that people accessing the JB-7 public walkway are trespassing on their private property since the town removed the original fence in 2023 due to safety concerns. The removal has left only vegetation as a barrier between the public path and the private land.

Colony resident Lori Hill described how the situation worsens during peak summer months when visitors arrive in large numbers seeking beach access. She explained that beachgoers push through bushes to reach the property, carrying coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs while parking throughout the day. Hill recalled that when the fence was in place, property boundaries were clear and easy to enforce. Now, residents frequently encounter trespassers and confrontations have become common. "We used to confront them and tell them this is private property, and they would get pretty rude," Hill said. "So, now what we've just been doing is just calling the police, and they've been coming up and confronting them."

The issue reached the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where officials acknowledged that the town has no obligation to install a fence. However, Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring more affordable options to address the problem. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. The council decided to include the fence question in budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

Not all beachgoers perceive the situation as problematic. Michael House, a visitor who walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot, said he has not witnessed the trespassing issues residents describe. "There's plenty of free parking," House said. "If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue, I have never noticed anyone hopping the fence or the shrubs or anything like that." Meanwhile, Hill expressed hope that the town would reinstall the fence to protect the residents' landscaping and private parking areas. The council's July 15 budget meeting will determine whether the town moves forward with any solution.

cards.headline: Woman dies in Hobe Sound house fire as community rallies around grieving fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
A Hobe Sound man is leaning on his community after losing his fiancée in a deadly home fire earlier this week. Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke about the loss and how she wants White to be remembered. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano. She was always the first to lend a hand. She loves kids, she loves her kids. She loves people," Fenn said. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak for those who knew her. "Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July. So, she passed just a few days before her birthday," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial Turnpike interchange. The move is part of the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. Samples said the interchange is about accessibility and keeping up with growth in the city, stating it is a way to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. According to the FDOT website, the second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which is still in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock to close Monday for $3 million renovation, nearly doubling slip capacity
cards.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The year-long project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be allowed to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section of the downtown Stuart dock to continue boarding passengers. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and his business. Boat captain Parker Fisher, who is based in Stuart, said the dock has needed work over the years and he is glad the city is investing in it.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem Blue Cross denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied coverage for breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before the scheduled procedure. Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield said the surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer stated is still considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated that the "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product gives her patients the least amount of complications. Despite the denial, Clark underwent reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. An Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and that Clark retains the right to appeal the decision.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home. Friends launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound that she shared with her fiancé, Mark. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation.

Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Nina Fenn, who has been White's friend for eight years, said she learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants, played the piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. She noted that the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he previously lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. The timing adds another layer of heartbreak, as White's birthday is the Fourth of July, just a few days after she passed away.

cards.headline: Autonomous transit company proposes elevated network connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. Palm Beach County commissioners will hear the proposal Tuesday.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system would also link the convention center and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, bypassing traffic congestion. The company estimates travel times of less than 10 minutes between downtown and the airport, seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport, and one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger emphasized the service would be priced like public transit rather than rideshare. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year as inflation hits holiday staples
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Inflation is driving the increase across multiple staple items. Ground beef prices are up 5.5%, while buns have risen 7.7%. Strawberries have been hit particularly hard by a Florida frost, jumping 12.4% in price. Ice cream prices are also up 5.3%.

Not all cookout ingredients carry higher price tags this year. Potato prices have declined, offering savings for those planning potato chips or salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends comparing stores to find the best deals and creating a meal plan to cut down food waste as ways to manage costs during the holiday.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is working hard during the summer months with ambitious goals for the 2026 fall season. Last year, the team finished with a 10-2 record and won the district championship, but a second-round playoff loss has motivated them to aim higher. The players and coaching staff believe a state title is within reach if they can extend their playoff run beyond where they finished last season.

Head coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of the senior class as a major advantage heading into the fall. Most of the seniors have been with the program for four years, with many coming up through the middle school system. This continuity means the senior leaders already understand the program's culture and have experienced success throughout their time with the Scots. Robertson expressed confidence that the senior class could lead the program to its best season yet.

The team's approach to improvement centers on raising the level of competition. Senior Jack Williams explained that the program intentionally scheduled tougher opponents this fall to push themselves and attract attention to the school. Rather than seeking easy wins, the Scots want to test themselves against strong teams. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that true success cannot be measured by an undefeated regular season alone. He said the priority must be advancing further in the playoffs, as winning in the regular season means little if the team continues to exit in the second round. The players have set a clear goal of progressing deeper into postseason play than they did last year.

The summer training period has become a source of motivation for the roster. Senior Edmyer St. Jean described the daily workouts as something meaningful to work toward, knowing that the effort invested now will translate to success when the season begins. The team is using the challenging summer schedule as fuel for their ambitious state title aspirations. With veteran leadership, a demanding schedule planned for the fall, and a commitment to postseason success, the Scots are preparing themselves for what they hope will be a breakthrough season in 2026.

cards.headline: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deploys two boats for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County maritime teams are on standby with two boats and medics positioned in the north and south as hundreds of boaters hit the water for the holiday weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected to hit Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting Martin County Maritime Response Unit to deploy two boats with medics on standby in both the north and south areas of the county. Lt. Brett Harry said his team is prepared to respond to a wide range of medical emergencies, from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious cardiac events, potential spinal injuries and other critical situations.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, are taking extra precautions on the water. Harry emphasized that boaters should keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and bring life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher suspended after controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009 who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Theobald's Facebook posts labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, contending that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney maintains that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk constituted a "serious offense" and that his removal was appropriate.

However, Livingstone's order issued last month cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling stating that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald returns to his position.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in Monday home fire as community rallies around fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home she shared with her fiancé Mark. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn reflected on White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, playing the piano, kids and people, and was always the first to lend a hand. The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with infrastructure improvements to address transportation needs in the growing community. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, noted that there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The partial interchange is designed to improve accessibility and accommodate growth that has already occurred and will continue over the next 20 to 50 years. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange project. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second phase, which will widen the road from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, which is currently in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, saw a nearly $7,000 lien removed from his home and unfinished roof repairs completed after WPTV investigated his complaint against Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran from Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof before hurricane season. He made six payments totaling more than $17,000 to the company but said workers left two holes unfinished on the back of his home and stopped responding to his calls, texts and emails starting in January. Letters from Gulfeagle Supply then warned that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien against his home, claiming the roofing contractor never paid for materials supplied to McCoy's property.

WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey spoke directly with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, who declined to comment on camera citing legal reasons. Within an hour of that conversation, Hussey returned to McCoy's home with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, officially lifting the lien. McCoy also learned the contractor would send someone to fix the two unfinished roof areas. About an hour later, McCoy sent WPTV a photo showing crews back on his roof completing the work.

cards.headline: Anthem Blue Cross denies breast cancer patient's reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance company deny coverage for breast reconstruction with GalaFlex mesh less than 24 hours before her scheduled surgery, though her plastic surgeon Dr. Alicia Billington found a way to complete the procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction using GalaFlex surgical mesh. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage, stating the procedure was "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh popular among plastic surgeons and FDA-approved for some uses in the body, but it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains considered off-label, investigational, and experimental. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated its "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives them "the least amount of complications" compared to other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Billington found a mechanism to proceed, and Clark received her reconstruction surgery a little more than a week ago. An Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they're based on medical evidence but stated the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction after investigative reporting. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach Hosts Fourth of July Fireworks and Pool Party with America 250 Events
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Season Programs Through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during sea turtle nesting season through September. The center said guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, the programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. Loggerhead Marinelife Center said its education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Secretary of State seeks to keep Republican candidate off ballot after incomplete qualifying papers
hero.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to bar Paula Stark from the House District 47 ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork by the June 12 qualifying deadline.
hero.body:
Paula Stark submitted her qualifying materials just 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12, and now Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking Leon Circuit Court to keep the St. Cloud Republican off the ballot. Five state employees provided sworn written declarations stating that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted the required Form 6 and did not receive it back when he turned in the rest of the paperwork during the final moments of the qualifying window. More than three weeks after the deadline, Stark still has not provided Form 6, according to a court disclosure by Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve.

Byrd challenged Stark's claims about a paperwork mix-up in his court response, suggesting she could have prevented the problem with more care. "Had Candidate Stark or Treasurer Davis exercised the slightest degree of care or prudence in the matter by questioning why the Form 6 was allegedly handed back, the mistake would have been discovered while Treasurer Davis was at the Division," Byrd wrote. He also noted that waiting until the last moment to file created unnecessary risk. Form 6 is a public disclosure form for financial interests. Reeve noted that Stark was one of 12 candidates who failed to properly submit Form 6, but half of those candidates corrected the problem and still qualified for the ballot.

Beyond the missing Form 6, Reeve documented a pattern of campaign finance problems. Stark's treasurer filed a campaign finance report more than one month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. In the 2022 and 2024 election cycles, audits found inconsistent transfers between accounts and balance problems. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines, with a remaining fine referred to debt collection for nonpayment.

The timing of this decision matters significantly. Byrd noted that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots due out between July 9 and 16. If Stark is removed from the ballot, the House District 47 primary would become an open contest between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. This would represent a major advantage for Florida Democrats, as the traditionally blue district representing parts of Osceola and Orange counties saw no other Republican candidates file to run. Byrd argued that reversing course at this stage would be costly and could create confusion in election results.

cards.headline: DeSantis allies accuse Lieutenant Governor's wife of operating anonymous accounts attacking Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts critical of Governor Ron DeSantis were suddenly deactivated Friday after prominent DeSantis communications veterans publicly accu.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations surfaced that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. The accusations came from prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team, including Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number and email address similar to those known to be used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication, which displayed messages to an email address with letters starred out and a phone number showing only the last digits. Pushaw identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that also appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw noted that the account content consisted entirely of posts promoting Jay Collins and attacking people who did not endorse him, including the governor. She pointed out that a member of a state board appointed by the same governor she was criticizing would presumably be too busy to maintain such accounts. Redfern posted that the FSUDude account was tied directly to Layla Collins' personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after the public accusations. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds for Governor. Florida Politics requested comments from Jay and Layla Collins.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg selects $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field site
cards.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid proposal to transform 58 acres around Tropicana Field into a mixed-use district centered on a 13-acre civic park and permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
St. Petersburg has selected The Burg Bid's $8.1 billion plan to redevelop Tropicana Field and the surrounding Historic Gas Plant District. Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, the proposal calls for purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the full land package valued at $405 million when factoring in $130 million in land the city would retain. A $20 million deposit would be required when a purchase and sale agreement is executed. The plan centers on Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central park that would anchor the district as a civic and cultural space. The park would be part of 18.5 acres of public park space and include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, cafe areas, public art and a concert lawn. The Woodson would serve as an anchor and civic landmark along the Legacy Link, a diagonal pedestrian corridor.

The proposal calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units in the Historic Gas Plant District and 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. Blue Sky Communities is the team's affordable and workforce housing partner. The district would be built in three main phases, each expected to take about five years, with early development beginning outside the Tropicana Field footprint before stadium demolition. The team's lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

cards.headline: Beachgoer killed by lightning strike while swimming in Florida
cards.teaser: A swimmer died after being struck by lightning at a Florida beach, with witnesses reporting the strike sounded like an atomic bomb.
cards.body:
A beachgoer was killed by a lightning strike while swimming in Florida, according to reports. Witnesses described the sound of the strike as resembling an atomic bomb going off. The incident occurred as Fourth of July celebrations were beginning across the state.

The deadly lightning strike highlights the dangers of Florida's frequent summer thunderstorms, particularly during outdoor holiday activities. Florida experiences some of the highest lightning activity in the nation during summer months.

cards.headline: New video released showing aftermath of deadly Florida alligator attack
cards.teaser: New video footage has been released showing the aftermath of a fatal alligator attack in Florida.
cards.body:
ABC News released new video showing the aftermath of a deadly alligator attack that occurred in Florida. The footage provides additional details about the fatal incident.

Alligator attacks remain rare in Florida despite the state's large alligator population. The release of aftermath video follows standard protocol in documenting wildlife incidents involving fatalities.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman killed in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home that investigators believe was caused by an electrical issue.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died in a house fire at her Hobe Sound home on Monday. Authorities discovered her body after flames consumed the residence. The sheriff's office has indicated that an electrical problem may have sparked the blaze, though the investigation into the cause remains ongoing.

White's fiancé, Mark, contacted her longtime friend Nina Fenn to inform her of the tragedy. Fenn, who had known White for eight years, learned of the death through that phone call. The community has rallied to support Mark during this difficult time. Friends organized a fundraiser to help him rebuild after the fire destroyed numerous belongings that he and White shared. Fenn described what she witnessed when she returned to the scene as "completely a state of devastation."

Fenn spoke about the person White was and how she wanted her to be remembered. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said. "She was always the first to lend a hand." Fenn also noted that White had a deep love for children and people in general. The loss carries additional weight for Mark, who had previously experienced profound tragedy. According to Fenn, Mark lost his only child, Jacob, in a tragic incident. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically," Fenn said. "So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him."

The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak for those who knew her. White's birthday was approaching on July 4, meaning she passed away just days before turning a year older. "Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July. So, she passed just a few days before her birthday," Fenn said. Despite the tragedy, Fenn emphasized that White's memory will continue to live on. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said.

Fire agencies extinguished a fire at an abandoned structure in Jensen Beach. Multiple agencies responded to the scene to battle the blaze.

The fire occurred at an abandoned building in Jensen Beach. Crews were able to bring the fire under control.

hero.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie
hero.teaser: Costco is planning to open its first store on the Treasure Coast in Port St. Lucie.
hero.body:
The warehouse retailer has announced plans for a Port St. Lucie location, marking the first Costco on the Treasure Coast. The store would serve St. Lucie County and surrounding areas. Port St. Lucie residents currently travel to Palm Beach County or other locations to shop at Costco. The new store represents a major retail addition for the city and the broader Treasure Coast region.

This expansion comes as Port St. Lucie continues significant infrastructure improvements to accommodate growth. The city is working on major road projects designed to handle both current congestion and future development. A $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is underway to expand the roadway and improve accessibility throughout the area. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the city recognizes the need to plan ahead. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to donate 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to support the interchange construction.

While the ongoing construction has been noticeable to residents, many recognize its value. Resident Erin Scheumeister acknowledged the inconvenience but supported the work. "They're still doing construction over there," she said. "It was like you couldn't get away from it." However, Scheumeister added, "We definitely needed it to be expanded. It'll be a lot better and easier to get to work." The combination of the Costco development and these infrastructure improvements positions Port St. Lucie for continued growth while addressing the transportation challenges that rapid expansion creates.

cards.headline: Body of missing diver found near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office recovered the body of a missing diver on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet.
cards.body:
Deputies reported finding the body of a missing diver on the Florida coast near Fort Pierce Inlet on Friday. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office handled the recovery operation.

The discovery concluded a search for the missing diver in waters off Fort Pierce. The incident occurred near the Fort Pierce Inlet, a popular diving location on the Treasure Coast.

cards.headline: Two people rescued after boat sinks in St. Lucie County Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Emergency responders rescued two people after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County on Thursday.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office responded to a boat sinking in the Intracoastal Waterway on Thursday afternoon. Two people were rescued from the water after their vessel went down.

Bodycam footage captured the rescue operation as deputies worked to pull the boaters to safety. The incident occurred in St. Lucie County waters along the Intracoastal Waterway, a major waterway running through the county.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $95 million Midway Road widening and Florida Turnpike interchange project
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is designed to help with congestion and safety while accommodating growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike, which is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman honored for supporting Little Free Libraries
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce resident received recognition for her work supporting Little Free Libraries in the community.
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce woman was honored for her contributions to Little Free Libraries, small book-sharing structures placed in neighborhoods. Her support has helped expand access to books in St. Lucie County.

Little Free Libraries allow residents to take books and share books with neighbors. The recognition highlights community efforts to promote literacy in Fort Pierce and surrounding areas.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Communities Mark America's 250th Anniversary with Celebrations and Fireworks
hero.body:
Communities across the Treasure Coast celebrated America's 250th anniversary on Saturday, July 4, 2026, with fireworks displays and Independence Day events. The milestone anniversary marked 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence in 1776.

Celebrations took place throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties as part of the nationwide commemoration. Fireworks displays were scheduled across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast region for the holiday weekend.

The 250th anniversary represents a significant milestone in American history, with communities nationwide hosting special events to mark the occasion. Local celebrations provided residents an opportunity to observe the historic anniversary with traditional Independence Day festivities.

The holiday fell on a Saturday this year, with most celebrations taking place on July 4. Communities across the region organized events to honor the anniversary while providing traditional Fourth of July entertainment for residents.

cards.headline: Fourth of July Cookout Costs Rise 4 Percent, Ground Beef and Strawberries Hit Hardest
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from last year, with ground beef up 5.5 percent and strawberries up 12.4 percent after a Florida frost.
cards.body:
The American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey reveals that Fourth of July traditions will cost more this year. A holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago. Ground beef prices increased 5.5 percent, while buns rose 7.7 percent. Strawberries experienced the steepest jump at 12.4 percent, attributed to a Florida frost, and ice cream prices increased 5.3 percent.

Not all cookout staples saw price increases. Potato prices dropped this year, offering relief to shoppers buying potato chips and salad ingredients. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends that families shop strategically by comparing prices across stores and creating meal plans to reduce food waste as they prepare for the holiday.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Schools Earn Third Consecutive A Rating from State
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third year in a row, with 84 percent of district schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, received an "A" or "B" rating, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record 93.5 percent graduation rate. District leaders reported that 86 percent of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. A total of 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years as principal after five years as assistant principal, said the school modified its early childhood curriculum program three years ago. Students who started in that program are now in third grade and performing at higher levels. Three other schools improved from "C" to "A" ratings: Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach Named Only Florida City to Win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, the only Florida city selected this year.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach received the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city among 10 U.S. communities to receive the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's community engagement efforts. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that the award reflects their heart and determination. "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents," Miller-Anderson said. "Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs: the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Juno Beach Fence Dispute at JB-7 Beach Access Could Cost Town Thousands
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
cards.body:
A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach access point in Juno Beach is creating tension between Colony Condos residents and summer beachgoers, with a potential fix costing the town thousands of dollars. The town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons, leaving only bushes to separate the public access path from private land. Colony resident Lori Hill said the problem peaks in summer, with people parking in private spots and cutting through bushes with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Hill said residents used to confront trespassers but noted that people would respond rudely, so residents have since called police to handle confrontations.

Not all beachgoers agree a problem exists. Michael House, who walks to JB-7 from a public lot a couple of blocks away, said he has not witnessed the issues residents describe. The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring a lower-cost solution, possibly combining split rail fencing with shrubs. The council agreed to address the fence question during its upcoming budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots Football Eyes State Title After 10-2 Season and District Championship
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title but a second-round playoff exit left the team aiming for a deeper postseason run.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district championship, but a second-round playoff exit has left them hungry for more. This offseason, the team is preparing for the 2026 fall season with their sights set on a state title. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson noted that most of the seniors are four-year veterans who came up through the middle school program and have experienced success throughout their careers. "Hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To reach that goal, the Scots are embracing a more demanding schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind the tougher slate of opponents: "We wanna compete and take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that." For the team, success this season will be measured by playoff performance. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that going undefeated in the regular season means little if the team continues losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily work in summer training serves as motivation, adding that the hard work "adds up every day as something like to look forward to" as they aim to "see the results when we come off the season positive and break our record."

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School Band to Represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march down the National Mall in Washington, D.C., on July 4 at 10:30 a.m., representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade as the only band representing Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the scale of the audience, saying "There are millions, if not billions, of people watching" and noting that while there is pressure, the team will rise to the occasion. She explained the physical demands of marching band, stating that students must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound without hearing the steps in their music. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is laser-focused on nailing every detail, emphasizing that everyone will be able to see what the Boca High band is capable of. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone said she has full confidence the students will put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing and said it showcases how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube.
